message.subject: Digital Study Resource: Mūlamadhyamakakārikā with 3D Visualizations
message.body:
Dear Dhamma friends,

I am sharing a guided study resource I have developed for approaching Nāgārjuna's Mūlamadhyamakakārikā through contemplative-science pedagogy.

Nagarjuna Quantum Reflections (https://mulamadhyamakarika-quanta.netlify.app/iks-conference) offers:

• Interactive 3D visualizations of dependent origination concepts
• ATOM Framework: Procedural animations for abstract verses
• Research Mode with epistemic transparency (guardrails against quantum mysticism)
• Multi-tiered scaffolding from introductory to advanced levels

This is intended as guided study support—not Dharma instruction—for those exploring Madhyamaka through a contemplative-science lens. The methodology emphasizes transparent framing and welcomes feedback on philosophical accuracy.

The project has a citable Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19282735

I welcome any reflections from this community on its approach, particularly regarding respectful engagement with the text.

With mettā,
Sanjay Bhargava

message.subject: [Resource] Madhyamaka Pedagogy Tool with Quantum Physics Parallels
message.body:
Hello Dharma friends,

I would like to share a digital humanities project developed for Madhyamaka study contexts.

Nagarjuna Quantum Reflections explores the Mūlamadhyamakakārikā through:

• 3D WebGL visualizations of śūnyatā and pratītyasamutpāda
• Structural parallels with quantum mechanics (superposition, relationality)
• Epistemic guardrails: "Research Mode" prevents quantum mysticism overreach
• Madhyamaka-first methodology: physics analogies serve philosophical clarity

The platform is designed for:
- Academic Madhyamaka courses
- Contemplative education programs
- Guided study groups (not replacement for lineage instruction)

Zenodo DOI for citation: 10.5281/zenodo.19282735
Academic showcase: https://mulamadhyamakarika-quanta.netlify.app/iks-conference

I particularly welcome feedback from this community on:
- Philosophical framing accuracy
- Suitability for Tibetan shedra contexts
- Potential for monastic science education

With gratitude,
Sanjay Bhargava

message.subject: Digital Quantum Physics Teaching Aid for Monastic Students
message.body:
Dear Karma Tenzin Khangsar,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to introduce a digital teaching resource that may complement the Emory-Tibet Science Initiative's quantum physics curriculum for monastic students.

Nagarjuna Quantum Reflections is an interactive web platform that uses 3D WebGL visualizations to teach quantum concepts through the lens of classical Indian epistemology—specifically Nāgārjuna's Mūlamadhyamakakārikā.

Why this might fit ETSI:
• Visualizes quantum superposition, entanglement, and complementarity through 3D animations
• Epistemic transparency: built-in guardrails against "quantum mysticism"
• Respects traditional contemplative frameworks while teaching modern physics
• Free white-label access available for monastic education contexts

I noticed ETSI's curriculum covers quantum mechanics, and thought this might provide an alternative pedagogical angle—particularly for students with strong background in Buddhist philosophy.

The project has a Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.19282735) for academic reference.

Academic showcase: https://mulamadhyamakarika-quanta.netlify.app/iks-conference
GitHub: https://github.com/sanjabh11/Mulamadhyamakakarika

Would you be open to a brief conversation about whether this might fit ETSI's pedagogical goals? I am happy to provide free institutional access for evaluation.

With warm regards,

Sanjay Bhargava
